title: £2.3m dual helipad completed at Bangor Hospital
summary: This development aims to strengthen emergency care for patients across North Wales.
body_markdown:
Construction of the new £2.3million dual helipad facility at Bangor Hospital (Ysbyty Gwynedd) has been completed, marking a significant milestone in a major development that will strengthen emergency care for patients across North Wales.


They are the first hospital helipads in Britain to be purpose built for search-and-rescue and air ambulance helicopters with funding from the HELP Appeal


The facility, funded by £1.5m from the HELP Appeal, the only charity in the U.K. dedicated to funding hospital helipads, alongside more than £800,000 provided by Welsh Government, became operational on Monday, Nov. 16.


The development replaces and upgrades the hospital’s former helipad, which was installed in 1997.


With aviation regulations and operational requirements having evolved, the new facility has been designed to meet current and future Civil Aviation Authority standards while supporting vital air ambulance and search and rescue operations.


Paul Andrew, director of operations for the West Integrated Health Community of Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board, welcomed the completion of construction and thanked those who have supported the development.


Andrew said: “It’s fantastic news that construction of our new dual helipad facility has now been completed.


“We are incredibly grateful to the HELP Appeal for its generous support and commitment to improving emergency care, as well as Welsh Government for its funding contribution. Without their support, this vital project would not have been possible.


“I would also like to thank everyone involved in bringing this development to fruition. It’s a fantastic investment in the future of emergency care in North Wales and one that will benefit patients, our clinical teams and emergency services for many years to come.”


The dual helipad will allow Wales Air Ambulance and HM Coastguard search-and-rescue helicopters to land simultaneously helping to reduce delays and strengthen the hospital’s response to major incidents and time-critical emergencies.


Dr. Pete Williams, clinical lead for Bangor Hospital’s Emergency Department, added:


“We are seeing an increasing number of patients arriving or being transferred by helicopter, and there are occasions when more than one aircraft needs access to the hospital at the same time. Although these situations are relatively uncommon, they can result in delays when every minute matters.


“Having two fully operational helipads will remove the risk of one aircraft having to wait for another to leave, improving efficiency and providing greater resilience during periods of high demand or major incidents.


“Ultimately, this development is about improving patient care and ensuring that people can access the right treatment as quickly and safely as possible.


“While most people will thankfully never need to use these facilities, they provide a vital safety net for those facing the most serious medical emergencies. It’s a fantastic development that will strengthen emergency care across North Wales for many years to come.”


Robert Bertram, chief executive of the HELP Appeal, added:


“This is a proud milestone for the HELP Appeal charity, not only are we helping to fund Britain’s first dual hospital helipads, it’s also our first project in Wales. It brings the number of helipads we have funded to 55, helping air ambulances bring critically ill patients closer to the specialist care they urgently need.


“We owe a huge thank you to our supporters. Their generosity has made this possible and will help patients for years to come.”


Dyfed Edwards, chair of Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board, said:


“The completion of this new dual helipad is an important milestone for the Health Board and a step forward in strengthening emergency care for communities across North Wales. I would like to thank the HELP Appeal and Welsh Government for their support in making this project possible.”


Deputy chief Coastguard John Craig said:


“We welcome the opening of the new helicopter landing site at Ysbyty Gwynedd. This new site enhances access for search-and-rescue helicopters and highlights the close working between emergency services organizations for communities across North Wales.”


Charlotte Phillips, Wales Air Ambulance director of aviation operations, said:


“As a Charity, our focus is on delivering the best possible service for our population, so any development that can help improve patient care is wholeheartedly welcomed.


“We thank the HELP Appeal and Welsh Government for their support for the new dual helipad at Ysbyty Gwynedd, as well as everyone at the hospital and Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board who has helped make this development possible.”


Mabon ap Gwynfor, cabinet minister for health and care, said:


“The new dual helipad at Ysbyty Gwynedd – the first of its kind in Britain – is now open and will make a real difference to outcomes for seriously ill and injured patients.


“I’m proud that Welsh Government has worked on this vital project alongside the health board and the HELP Appeal.”


*This press release was prepared and distributed by the HELP Appeal.*
